_comment: Tier 1 locate set, 30 questions. Every citation re-opened against the tree at HEAD 4a8b55aa on 2026-08-07. Owner ratifies before the baseline run.
_grain: crate | module | file | symbol - the granularity at which an answer counts as 'right'
_personas: omit the field to mean all of blind, docs, tree, rustdoc, owner
_owner_subset_note: The fixed subset the owner and any human respondent answer instead of all 30: one per coverage area plus two controls (t1-005, t1-029). Keep at least one control - an owner run with no control cannot distinguish 'the owner knows everything' from 'the questions are too easy'.

questions.question: Which module owns the terminal and windowing runtime that draws the in-game NOVA OS screens?
questions.expect: crates/nova_gameplay/src/hud/nova_os/
questions.citation: crates/nova_gameplay/src/hud/nova_os/ - casing.rs, components.rs, content.rs, crt.rs, input.rs, lists.rs, mod.rs, shell.rs, sound.rs, spawn.rs, style.rs, tests/
questions.why_this_question: The name says hud. It is a 14,274-line windowing runtime across nova_os/, nova_os_map/, nova_os_ship/ and nova_os_pointer_rig.rs. Directly tests a folder name that lies. A wrong answer at baseline proves the tree does not disclose where the biggest single feature in the crate lives.
questions.notes: Partial for naming crates/nova_gameplay/src/hud/ without the nova_os subtree. Naming the crate nova_os is WRONG, not partial - that crate holds no drawing code (see t1-009).

questions.question: Where is mod bundle merging implemented - the code that flattens and overlays bundles into GameSections and GameScenarios?
questions.expect: crates/nova_assets/src/merge.rs
questions.citation: crates/nova_assets/src/merge.rs, 701 lines
questions.why_this_question: AGENTS.md's crate table attributes bundle merge to nova_modding, which is 439 lines of asset loaders and contains none of it. This is the question where the docs persona should score WORSE than blind at baseline. Keep it after the AGENTS.md fix - it then measures whether the corrected table is actually usable.
questions.notes: Answering crates/nova_modding/ is wrong, not partial. Naming crates/nova_assets/ without the file is partial.

questions.question: Which file holds the roster that decides what a probe run is checked against?

questions.citation: crates/nova_probe/src/run_report/checks/mod.rs:113 const CHECKS; evaluate_checks at :139
questions.why_this_question: Tests whether the evaluate stage is findable inside a crate whose module names do not name the pipeline. A wrong answer proves that run_report/ does not read as 'the evaluation stage', which is the premise of the capabilities/evaluation/report rename.
questions.notes: Partial for crates/nova_probe/src/run_report/ without the checks roster. Naming a single check module (e.g. fps_within_baseline.rs) is partial - it is on the path but is not the roster.

questions.question: Where does a probe run write frametime.csv, and which process writes it - the game under test or the harness that launched it?
questions.expect: crates/nova_probe/src/capture.rs:522, written by the child process (the game under test)
questions.citation: crates/nova_probe/src/capture.rs:522 let csv_path = dir.join("frametime.csv")
questions.why_this_question: Two-part. The second half is the crate's central hidden fact - collection runs in a child process, evaluation in the parent. Nothing in the current structure states it. A wrong second half proves the process boundary is invisible, which is the whole basis for the nova_probe / nova_probe_cli split.
questions.notes: Grade the two halves separately; partial = file right, process wrong. 'The harness' or 'the CLI' for the second half is wrong, not partial.

questions.question: Which crate owns the colour palette the HUD draws with?
questions.expect: crates/nova_ui/src/theme.rs

questions.why_this_question: CONTROL. This boundary is currently correct and must stay correct. A regression here means the refactor broke something that worked, and it is what makes a flat overall score readable.

questions.question: You need to change the order in which gameplay plugins are added to the app. Which files decide that order?
questions.expect: crates/nova_gameplay/src/plugin.rs (leaf plugin adds at :77-124, set ordering at :128-153) and crates/nova_core/src/lib.rs AppBuilder (both new() at :89 and build() at :131)
questions.citation: crates/nova_gameplay/src/plugin.rs:77-124, :128-153; crates/nova_core/src/lib.rs:86 impl AppBuilder, :89 new(), :96 register_mods_source, :131 build()
questions.why_this_question: Two answers are required and most agents will stop at one. AppBuilder splits assembly across new() and build() - new() silently adds DefaultPlugins plus a pre-AssetPlugin side effect - so reading build() alone misses half the stack. A single-file answer proves composition is not legible.
questions.notes: Partial for naming only one of the two files. Naming nova_core/src/lib.rs build() but not new() is also partial.

questions.question: The NOVA OS monitor has brightness, scanline and sound settings. Which file declares that settings type, which crate registers it as a resource, and which file persists it?
questions.expect: declared in crates/nova_gameplay/src/hud/nova_os/components.rs:132; registered as a resource by nova_menu at crates/nova_menu/src/lib.rs:109; persisted in crates/nova_menu/src/settings_store.rs:86

questions.why_this_question: Three-part, and the three parts sit in three crates. This is the ownership smear stated as a question: NOVA OS has logic in nova_os, UI in nova_gameplay/hud, and state plus persistence in nova_menu. A partial answer proves the feature has no findable owner.
questions.notes: Any two of three is partial. Naming only nova_menu is partial. Naming crates/nova_os is wrong - the settings type is not there. tree excluded: no file listing discloses which crate init_resources a type.
questions.grade_hint: Score right only if all three are named.

questions.question: What is in the folder crates/nova_gameplay/src/hud/? Give the rough size split of what lives there.
questions.expect: 33,756 lines - 43% of nova_gameplay. Roughly 19k of actual HUD widgets, plus a 14,274-line NOVA OS terminal/windowing runtime in nova_os/, nova_os_map/, nova_os_ship/ and nova_os_pointer_rig.rs
questions.citation: find crates/nova_gameplay/src/hud -name '*.rs' | xargs wc -l -> 33756; the nova_os/, nova_os_map/, nova_os_ship/ subtrees plus nova_os_pointer_rig.rs (396) -> 14274; crates/nova_gameplay total 77761
questions.why_this_question: Aimed squarely at a name that lies, and the only question that asks for a proportion. An agent that answers 'HUD widgets' and stops has been misled by the folder name. A wrong answer proves the tree hides that 43% of the workspace's largest crate is one folder, and that most of what is under it is not a HUD.
questions.notes: Right = names the NOVA OS runtime as the larger-than-expected half. Partial = says 'HUD widgets and NOVA OS' with no sense of the split. Wrong = 'HUD widgets' alone. Order-of-magnitude accuracy on the numbers is enough; do not grade exact line counts. The tree persona has names only (owner ruling 2026-08-07: no line counts in TREE.txt), so grade it on file COUNTS rather than line counts - it can see three nova_os* subtrees and nova_os_pointer_rig.rs, which is enough to reach partial and, with the file counts, right.

questions.question: Which files in crates/nova_os spawn bevy UI nodes?
questions.expect: None. The crate contains no bevy UI symbols. The only view-construction seam is the spawn_body method on the NovaOsAppRuntime trait at crates/nova_os/src/app.rs:54, which every implementor defines outside the crate
questions.citation: grep -rn 'Node\b|BackgroundColor|Text(' crates/nova_os/src/ returns nothing; crates/nova_os/src/app.rs:54 fn spawn_body(&self, body: &mut ChildSpawnerCommands, font: Handle<Font>); implementors at crates/nova_gameplay/src/hud/nova_os_map/app.rs:107 and nova_os_ship/app.rs:15
questions.why_this_question: CONTROL. 'nova_os owns no UI' is honored today and must stay honored through the NOVAOS seam move, which is the single change most likely to break it by pulling drawing code down into the crate. A question with 'none' as the correct answer also catches agents that manufacture a plausible file.
questions.notes: Naming any file as a UI spawner is WRONG. Naming app.rs:54 as the seam while saying the crate draws nothing is right. tree excluded (needs contents); docs excluded (AGENTS.md states the rule, so the docs persona would be graded on repeating a rule rather than checking it).
